children: Indonesia's trade surplus was likely sustained in August, supported by the unwinding of nickel export delays and possible frontloading of coal, palm oil and nickel shipments ahead of stricter government export reporting requirements from Sept. 1, Maybank analysts Brian Lee and Chua Hak Bin say in a note. However, higher oil prices and robust capital-goods imports could widen the drag on the trade balance, they say. Rising domestic biodiesel demand and potential El Nino-related disruptions may also constrain exports, they add. Maybank raises its 2026 current-account deficit forecast for Malaysia to 2% of GDP from 1% projected earlier. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
